Review support of each cell: is more validation worth it?

Source: R/post_validation.R
review_support.Rd

For each site x species cell (and each level of the by columns, such as the bin of an environmental gradient or of an acoustic index), counts the reviewed clips at high scores, their precision, and the high-score detections of the selection tables that were not reviewed, and labels the cell:

Usage

review_support(
  validation,
  detections,
  conf_high = 0.7,
  min_n = 15,
  min_precision = 0.5,
  target_precision = 0.9,
  by = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  occasion_unit = c("file", "minute"),
  remap_from = NULL,
  remap_to = NULL
)

Arguments

validation

Reviewed clips, as for precision_by_bin() (the validation_by_clip.csv tables).

detections

Predictions, as returned by read_selection_tables().

conf_high

Score from which a prediction counts as high.

min_n

Minimum number of clips, as in suggest_thresholds(), and of unreviewed high-score detections for "review more".

min_precision

Precision at high scores below which a cell is "unreliable".

target_precision

Target precision of suggest_thresholds().

by

Optional columns that split each cell, e.g. "temp_bin". They must be columns of covariates (joined to both tables) or of both tables.

covariates

Optional table of occasion covariates, such as the output of covariate_bins(), joined to the clips and to the predictions by the columns it shares with them among site, night, recording_date, recording_hour, source_audio and occasion_id, as in select_clips().

occasion_unit

The occasion of the occupancy model: "file" (the whole recording) or "minute" (minute of the file, from file_offset).

remap_from, remap_to

Replace the prefix remap_from of the begin_path paths by remap_to, e.g. "N:/" and "/Volumes/Arara/". Backslashes are turned into forward slashes first.

Value

A tibble with site, species_folder, the by columns, n_reviewed, n_fp (false positives among them), n_high (reviewed clips with score >= conf_high), prec_high (their precision), n_high_all (predictions with score >= conf_high), unreviewed_high, threshold and diagnosis, ordered by diagnosis.

Details

  • "reached": suggest_thresholds() found a threshold that reaches target_precision with at least min_n clips;

  • "exhausted": fewer than min_n high-score detections are left to review, so more effort cannot add support;

  • "unreliable": precision at high scores is below min_precision, so more review would only confirm it (retrain the classifier instead);

  • "review more": high-score detections remain and precision there is intermediate, so a further round of review may reach a threshold;

  • "not reviewed": the cell has detections but no reviewed clip.

The cut-offs (conf_high, min_n, min_precision) are illustrative defaults: set them from the precision the study needs. Splitting cells by by lowers the number of clips per cell, so more cells fall short of min_n; compare with the reading without by. These labels interpret counts; they are not a statistical test.

See also

vignette("validation-effort").
